title: A signed change is the negative of a decrease
spoken: Mass after minus mass before equals negative L divided by c squared.
explanation: For emission, L is positive but the signed body-mass change is negative. This concerns the body that lost the light; the energy has not vanished from a larger system containing body and radiation.
assumptions: Two equal, opposite light pulses remove total positive energy L; their symmetry removes recoil in the body’s rest frame.
The two inertial descriptions refer to the same emission and the same body boundary; |v| < c.
These are authored modern teaching equations, not a transcription or printed-notation concordance.
The relation H − E = K + C uses the same unknown additive C before and after emission. This is a premise; conservation and subtraction do not prove it.
Δm is defined as after minus before, whereas the decrease magnitude is before minus after.

notes.title: Emitted energy L
notes.explanation: Total energy of both opposite pulses, in the body’s rest frame. It is not the body’s unknown total energy.

notes.title: Modern SI speed of light
notes.explanation: c denotes the speed of light in modern SI notation. A normalized model with c = 1 is a different unit convention and cannot supply values labeled metres per second.

notes.title: Square the speed of light
notes.explanation: The squared SI speed supplies the energy-to-mass conversion, not an arbitrary numerical scaling.

notes.title: Convert the emitted energy
notes.explanation: L/c² is the positive magnitude of the mass decrease for the same body boundary.

notes.title: After minus before
notes.explanation: Δm is the signed change: mass after minus mass before. Emission of positive L therefore gives a negative value. It is not the positive decrease magnitude.

notes.title: Reverse the subtraction order
notes.explanation: Changing from before-minus-after to after-minus-before reverses the sign. Positive emission therefore makes this signed change negative.

notes.title: What this relation asserts
notes.explanation: For emission, L is positive but the signed body-mass change is negative. This concerns the body that lost the light; the energy has not vanished from a larger system containing body and radiation.

sentence.text: Mass after minus mass before equals negative L divided by c squared.
